findings.source_claim: After defining phi^N=(N lambda_N t)^(-1) E sum_(0<tau_n<=t) delta_Yn, the next identity uses lambda_N t phi^N Q and starts the sum at n=0, with tau_0=0.
hypotheses: Initial distribution is the actual ordinary-time stationary law psi^N
findings.decisive_evidence: Testing against 1 yields lambda_N t on the left and N lambda_N t+1 on the right. Difference (N-1)lambda_N t+1>0. This is exact for the stipulated process; no particle simulation or assumed numerical rate.
findings.proof: Report Section 3: restore N and start at n=1. Markov conditioning gives N lambda_N t phi^N Q=E sum_(n>=1) 1_(tau_n<=t) delta_Y_(n+1). Subtract the defining measure; pathwise telescoping has total variation at most2, including zero-jump paths. Thus ||phi^N Q-phi^N||<=2/(N lambda_N t)->0, and stationary marked-point intensity makes phi^N independent of t.
findings.impact: The displayed equality is false, but the full required stationarity conclusion follows under unchanged hypotheses. The later per-particle Green identity xi^N=lambda_N varpi^N G is correctly normalized and remains unchanged.

problems.source_claim_scope: The finite-measure stationarity display in the proof of Proposition 2.3 on acquired arXiv v1 PDF p.10; not the subsequent per-particle Green identity.
problems.independent_reasoning: With the stipulated ordinary-time stationary law and N>=12, the mean positive jump count is N lambda_N t and Q1=1. The printed left mass is lambda_N t but its n>=0 sum includes tau_0=0 and therefore has mass N lambda_N t+1. The strict positive difference (N-1)lambda_N t+1 proves failure without simulated trajectories or an assumed numerical intensity. Conditioning at each tau_n is valid since {tau_n<=t} belongs to its stopping-time sigma field. With N restored and n starting at 1, the difference from the defining sum is delta_(Y_(K_t+1))-delta_(Y_1) on K_t>=1 and zero on K_t=0, with total variation at most 2. Finite expected counts permit exchanging the sum and expectation. Stationarity makes the Palm law independent of integer t, and division by N lambda_N t and t tending to infinity proves invariance under Q.
problems.counterevidence_and_impact: The corrected proof establishes precisely the required conclusion under unchanged hypotheses. Proposition 2.4 uses per-particle intensity and remains xi^N=lambda_N varpi^N G; the correction must not add N there. The test by 1 is on finite measures, not an assertion that 1 is in the killed generator domain. This supports Minor and no conclusion against the main selection theorem.
